details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:6962-6985 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_6]
  PROBLEM: Backlog persistence occurs before waiver persistence, so a waiver-write failure can leave advisory backlog entries without matching waivers and cause later audits to deduplicate and lose the still-unfiled findings.
  WHY: Qwen rated this BLOCKER, while Moonshot rated it NIT because deterministic keys allow recovery through re-security-pass; the highest severity is used.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5823-5824 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The advisory body generator uses `[0-9-a-f]`, whose dash creates an unintended ASCII range and allows non-hex characters in `head_sha`.
  WHY: Crafted non-hex values can pass body-generation validation and produce provenance metadata that downstream validation rejects.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5823 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The advisory body generator accepts only exactly 40-character hashes while the audit engine accepts 40-64-character hashes.
  WHY: SHA-256 repositories with 64-character commit IDs cause deferred advisory generation to abort and leave follow-up state pending indefinitely.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5635-5647 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: Poller-side waiver-key validation checks only the `sha256:` prefix and total length instead of requiring 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.
  WHY: A malformed key can be treated as non-matching rather than rejected, creating inconsistent validation with the audit engine.
- scripts/security_audit.sh:1519-1574 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_6]
  PROBLEM: Deleting an authorization helper in a different function from the cited sink can fall through causal-diff analysis to blame ownership and be classified as base-owned.
  WHY: The project-introduced authorization bypass is routed to advisory findings instead of remaining a blocking security-pass finding.
- tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py:454-457 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: `_test_waiver_key` constructs test keys with `sha256(file:line:category)` instead of the production JSON payload containing the provenance commit.
  WHY: Tests can remain internally consistent while failing to detect regressions in production waiver-key composition.
- moonshotai_kimi-k3: create_security_pass_advisory_followup (~line 5746, the `[[ "${waiver_match_key}" =~ ^sha256:... ]] || return 0` early return) plus the settle jq in security_pass_file_deferred_advisory_followups (~line 6020, `if .waiver_match_key == $key`) | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k3]
  PROBLEM: Legacy deferred waiver rows without `waiver_match_key` are skipped by follow-up filing and cannot be settled.
  WHY: In-flight rows remain `followup_pending: true` and are retried indefinitely without an advisory issue being filed.
- scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py:67 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Generated advisories authored by a PAT whose association is `CONTRIBUTOR` are rejected by the trusted-association gate.
  WHY: Legitimate automated advisories from a contributor-associated PAT fail both plan-time and implement-time guards and remain unprocessed.
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:1627-1633 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k3]
  PROBLEM: The generated-advisory plan-time check is skipped in the source `coding-workflows` repository.
  WHY: Generated advisory plans targeting this repository are detected only at implement time rather than receiving the same plan-time enforcement as consumer repositories.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:4768 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `security_pass_rebind_if_no_new_project_lines` declares `local merge_base_sha="$2"` but never uses it.
  WHY: The passed argument has no runtime effect and obscures that the rebind logic relies on `default_sha` resolved from `$default_ref`.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5635 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The embedded waiver-processing Python parses `sys.argv[3]` into `_line_window` but never uses it.
  WHY: A non-integer legacy compatibility argument can still raise `ValueError` and abort the waiver-suppression batch despite the value being semantically unused.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh, Line or code reference: 5824 (`if not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9-a-f]{40}", head_sha):`) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The regex character class `[0-9-a-f]` is interpreted by Python as a range and accepts non-hex characters.
  WHY: Crafted values can pass validation and be embedded in advisory provenance metadata that downstream validation rejects.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh, Line or code reference: 5824 (advisory body) vs scripts/security_audit.sh:1414 (`re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{40,64}", audit_scope_head_sha)`) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The advisory body generator accepts exactly 40 hex characters while the audit engine accepts 40-64.
  WHY: SHA-256 commit IDs cause advisory generation to abort and leave deferred follow-up state pending.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh, Line or code reference: 4768 (`security_pass_rebind_if_no_new_project_lines <head_sha> <merge_base_sha> <default_ref>`) | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `merge_base_sha` is declared but never referenced.
  WHY: No runtime failure occurs, but the unused argument obscures which value controls the rebind window.
- scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py, Line or code reference: 67 (`TRUSTED_AUTHOR_ASSOCIATIONS = frozenset({"OWNER", "MEMBER", "COLLABORATOR"})`) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Generated advisories from a PAT associated as `CONTRIBUTOR` are rejected.
  WHY: The plan and implement guards treat legitimate automated advisories as invalid and leave them unprocessed.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh, Line or code reference: 5638-5643 (embedded waiver_for Python) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `waiver_for` validates only the `sha256:` prefix and length, not hexadecimal content.
  WHY: Malformed keys are treated as non-matching and can cause findings believed waived by the engine to remain blocking.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh, Line or code reference: 5635 (`_line_window = int(sys.argv[3])`) | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The parsed line-window argument is unused.
  WHY: A non-integer legacy argument can raise `ValueError` and abort waiver processing.

- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh, Line or code reference: create_security_pass_advisory_followup (~line 5746, the `[[ "${waiver_match_key}" =~ ^sha256:... ]] || return 0` early return) plus the settle jq in security_pass_file_deferred_advisory_followups (~line 6020, `if .waiver_match_key == $key`) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Legacy deferred waiver rows without `waiver_match_key` cannot have advisory follow-ups filed or settled.
  WHY: Such rows remain `followup_pending: true` and are retried indefinitely.
- scripts/security_audit.sh, Line or code reference: finding_is_project_owned causal-diff block (~lines 1519-1574): the `if has_deletion and not has_context_name: return True` guard followed by blame fallback | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: A deleted guard or helper in a different function from the cited sink is not kept blocking.
  WHY: The unchanged sink can fall through to blame and be routed to advisory findings despite a project-introduced bypass.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh, Line or code reference: advisory routing in run_security_pass_inline (~lines 6962-6985): backlog persist → security_pass_record_waivers → post_state_comment sequence | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: Backlog persistence precedes waiver persistence.
  WHY: A transient persistence failure creates inconsistent state and requires re-security-pass recovery.
- .github/workflows/plan.yml, Line or code reference: the generated-advisory guard block (~lines 1627-1633) inside the `Guard plans targeting template-owned paths` step, whose step-level `if` includes `!endsWith(github.repository, '/coding-workflows')` | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The plan-time generated-advisory check is skipped in the source repository.
  WHY: Enforcement occurs one phase later at implement time.
- HARDENING_SUGGESTION: tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py, Location: _test_waiver_key helper (~lines 451-466)
  Issue: The test helper builds keys as sha256("file:line:category"), while production builds sha256 of a JSON array [file, normalized_category, line, provenance_commit].
  Suggested minimal fix: Recompute one expected key using the production JSON payload shape and assert the engine-emitted key matches it.
- HARDENING_SUGGESTION: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh, Location: security_pass_apply_waivers_to_findings embedded Python, waiver_for (~lines 5635-5640)
  Issue: The poller-side key check validates only the "sha256:" prefix and total length 71.
  Suggested minimal fix: Replace the prefix/length check with the same re.fullmatch(r"sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}", key) used elsewhere.
